Twelve words are the whole setup now, Click'n'Load buttons reach an instance running anywhere, and the extension carries the same design language as everything else KnightLoader ships.

This is the first release since 1.1.0, and almost nothing about the extension is the same. Most people never need this download: **Settings > Browser & App** serves the copy embedded in whatever instance they are running. This build is for a browser store submission and for anyone who wants a fixed version to keep.

## ✨ Added

- **Click'n'Load, in the browser.** A site's own Click'n'Load button hands its links to a download manager on the same machine, at a fixed loopback port. That has never worked when KnightLoader runs on a NAS or a server, because a container's `127.0.0.1` is not the browser's. The extension now catches the submission inside the page, decodes it, and sends the links to whichever instance you pick, wherever it runs. **On from the first second**, because it is the reason most people install this at all.
- **The connection phrase is the entire configuration.** Paste the twelve words your instances already share and this browser joins the group. No address, no name, no password, no account. Every instance in the group appears, including ones your browser has no route to on its own.
- **The group as instance cards**, the same card the web UI's own Instances tab draws, in the popup, the send-to window and the options page. The default carries a **Standard** badge, and a right-click on another card moves it.
- **The look, in full.** Theme, corners, accent and the rainbow, each on its own card, with a colour picker the page draws itself, editable palette positions, and a switch that adopts corners, colours and the rainbow from your default instance.
- **42 languages**, following the browser by default.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The options page is one card per thing.** Remote access, Language, Look, Theme, Corners, Colours, Click'n'Load, Problems. Every explanation is an info bubble on the control it explains, rather than a paragraph of grey prose above the controls anyone came for.
- **Every switch is a real toggle**, and the language list is a real listbox with flags — no native checkbox, no native dropdown, no native colour input anywhere on the page.
- **The connection phrase is masked**, with an eye to check what was pasted. Twelve words open every instance in the group, which makes them a credential and not a setting.
- **A diagnostic report you can paste into an issue**, carrying the version, the browser, the language, the look, how many instances answered and how many Click'n'Load scripts are actually registered — and no address, no token and no key.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Click'n'Load could switch itself off on a browser restart.** "Nothing stored means on" was written one way in the install path and the options page, and the other way in the startup path, so a profile that never received the install-time write came back with the content scripts unregistered while the switch still read "on".
- **Rainbow mode did nothing visible.** It was stored, applied to the document and reported correctly, while every badge on the page went on taking the single accent, because nothing but the instance cards owned a palette position.

## 📋 Notes

- **This release requires access to websites, and that is new.** Click'n'Load means running code inside the page that carries such a button, and such a button can be on any site, so the set cannot be narrowed in advance. It was optional once, requested only when the feature was switched on; that was a better story for a reviewer and a worse product, because a switch reading "on" while quietly waiting for a permission dialog is a lie about what the extension is doing. Switching the feature off in the options **unregisters both content scripts** — `chrome.scripting.getRegisteredContentScripts()` returns `[]` and nothing of this extension runs in any page until it is switched back on.
- **The package is byte-identical to `extension/src` in the repository.** The download from a running instance used to bake that instance's address into a configuration file; the file is gone, because the extension holds no addresses at all any more. Anyone can build this zip from a checkout and compare it.
- **No account, no server of ours, no tracking.** The phrase never leaves the browser: what travels is a key derived from it by a one-way hash, and the relay that carries the traffic is never given the second key everything is encrypted with.
